summary: REPRODUCTION-ONLY pass (no fixes applied per instructions). Successfully and reliably REPRODUCED the consent-screen 'stuck requiring re-taps' bug for BOTH brand-new Account A and Account B (2/2 repro rate). Root cause identified with high confidence: a LanguageOnboardModal overlay renders on top of /consent immediately after signup and silently intercepts the user's first taps on the age-radio/checkboxes. The checkbox-state-inheritance concern (B inheriting A's choices) was investigated and NOT reproduced -- B's consent form always starts correctly unchecked (local component state, never shared across accounts).

ui_bugs.issue: Modal overlay renders on top of the /consent screen immediately after signup, blocking taps on consent-age-adult / consent-terms-checkbox / consent-data-checkbox. Verified: clicking consent-age-adult WHILE the modal was visible left state unchanged (age/terms/data all stayed 'false'). Only after dismissing the modal (tapping its own 'Continue in English' button) did taps on the real consent screen register.

integration_issues.issue: signup.tsx navigates to '/state?onboarding=1' after registration. Neither LanguageOnboardModal's EXCLUDED_PATHS (['/consent','/language','/login','/register','/welcome']) nor ConsentGuard's exclude-list (['language','consent','emergency']) exclude '/state'. During this transient /state render, LanguageOnboardModal's useEffect fires (user is set, checkedRef.current is false, pathname='/state' is NOT excluded) -> it sets checkedRef.current = true (permanently, for the lifetime of the app session) and shows the modal (visible=true) because the user has never completed language onboarding. Almost simultaneously, ConsentGuard also fires on '/state' and redirects to '/consent' because the user has no stored consent version. Because LanguageOnboardModal is rendered unconditionally as a sibling in _layout.tsx (not gated by route) and checkedRef.current is now permanently true, the modal keeps showing on top of /consent, blocking it.

react_native_issues.issue: Modal is declared 'intentionally non-dismissible' (onRequestClose is a no-op) and its full-screen semi-transparent overlay captures touches, so it fully blocks interaction with whatever screen is rendered underneath it -- in this case the legally-required consent screen. A user could tap the real continue button 'through' the overlay zero times; every tap during this window is consumed by the modal's own hit area (or silently swallowed if tapping outside the modal's sheet but still within its full-screen overlay).

rca_of_issue: Confirmed root cause: /app/frontend/src/components/LanguageOnboardModal.tsx line 50 EXCLUDED_PATHS = ['/consent','/language','/login','/register','/welcome'] is missing '/state' (and arguably '/signup'). signup.tsx (line 40) does router.replace('/state?onboarding=1') right after registration succeeds. On that transient render, LanguageOnboardModal's useEffect (lines 72-82) sees pathname='/state' which does NOT match any EXCLUDED_PATHS prefix, so it proceeds past the guard, sets checkedRef.current=true (one-time latch, never re-checked for the rest of the mounted session), reads the per-user AsyncStorage key 'lang_onboarded_v1_<userId>' (not yet set for a brand-new user), and calls setVisible(true). Concurrently, ConsentGuard in _layout.tsx (lines 76-86) also fires on '/state' (its own exclude-list only skips 'language'/'consent'/'emergency', not 'state'), finds no stored consent version for the new user, and does router.replace('/consent'). The net result: the app lands on /consent with the LanguageOnboardModal already latched to visible=true, and because checkedRef.current is already true it will never re-evaluate (so simply adding '/consent' exclusion wouldn't even help once the latch has already fired on /state). The modal overlay (full-screen, non-dismissible by backdrop tap, elevation/zIndex via React Native Modal) sits visually and interactively on top of the consent Pressables underneath. Steps to reproduce (100% repeatable, verified live twice): 1) Fresh browser/account -> Sign up with name/email/phone/password -> submit. 2) App briefly shows /state, then /consent?mode=update. 3) The 'Choose your language' bottom-sheet modal is already showing on top of the consent screen. 4) Tapping the age radio / checkboxes underneath does nothing (verified via aria-checked staying 'false' after a forced click). 5) Only after tapping the modal's own 'Continue in <language>' button (dismissing it) do the real consent checkboxes start responding to taps. This exactly matches the previously-flagged symptom 'gets stuck requiring re-taps on the consent Continue button' -- the user is actually tapping an invisible-in-intent-but-rendered-on-top modal first, unaware, and their first 1-2 taps are consumed by it.
verified_not_a_bug: Account B's consent form (age radio / Terms checkbox / Data checkbox) always initializes to false/false/false on mount -- NOT inherited from Account A. This is because consent.tsx uses local useState, freshly initialized on every mount, and is never pre-populated from any shared/global store.
consent-continue-button is correctly disabled (aria-disabled=true) until age='18+' AND termsTicked AND dataTicked are all true -- verified for both A and B.

Once the LanguageOnboardModal is dismissed, the underlying consent screen's own handleContinue logic works correctly on a SINGLE tap -- it is not the consent screen's debounce/submitting.current logic that is broken; the extra 'tap' users experience is consumed entirely by the modal overlay, not by any bug in consent.tsx itself.

Server-side consent/terms persistence works correctly across sessions: re-logging in as Account A in a brand-new browser context (AsyncStorage cleared) did NOT re-prompt /consent, confirming the backend-side terms_version check correctly recognises prior acceptance independent of local device storage.
action_items: Fix LanguageOnboardModal.tsx: add '/state' (and ideally '/signup') to EXCLUDED_PATHS, OR better -- re-check path exclusion on every pathname change instead of latching checkedRef.current permanently once a non-excluded path is seen, so that if the user is redirected to /consent immediately after, the modal check is correctly skipped.
Consider also gating ConsentGuard the same way, or ordering the two effects so ConsentGuard's ownership of /consent takes priority before LanguageOnboardModal's visibility check ever runs.

Defensive fix: even with correct path exclusion, consider adding a global check 'do not render LanguageOnboardModal while pathname starts with /consent' directly in LanguageOnboardModal's render (not just the one-time check effect), so a stale latch can never cause the modal to persist on top of the legally-required consent screen.

Minor (unrelated, lower priority): bottom-tab text selectors ('Rights', 'My files', 'Me') resolved to multiple DOM matches during navigation testing in this session -- recommend adding more specific/unique testIDs to the bottom tab bar buttons themselves (distinct from any same-named inline page content) to make future navigation tests unambiguous.
critical_code_review_comments: LanguageOnboardModal.tsx: the one-shot 'checkedRef.current = true' latch combined with a path-exclusion check that runs only once creates a race condition with any screen that briefly routes through a non-excluded intermediate path (here, '/state') before landing on an excluded one ('/consent'). One-shot latches guarding async side effects should re-validate the guard condition at the point the async result resolves, not just at effect-trigger time.

Both LanguageOnboardModal and ConsentGuard independently inspect `pathname`/`segments` against two DIFFERENT hard-coded exclude lists for conceptually the same 'don't interrupt these sensitive screens' rule. This duplication is itself a latent bug source (as proven here) -- a single shared constant/allowlist used by both guards would prevent this class of issue.
